Marissa / Neha — draft answers below; please review. I included links to the hosted docs and attached the redacted SOC 2 Type II and a small dataflow png we can share. Key points:

1) Model training: Redwood does NOT train or fine-tune public or internal production models on customer prompts or responses by default. We maintain a strict separation: customer prompt/response data is treated as customer-owned inference data.
- Optional opt-in: For select research collaborations (explicit, NDA'd projects) customers may opt-in to share de-identified telemetry for aggregated model improvement; this is never enabled without a signed agreement and explicit checkbox per account.

2) Retention: default retention window for hosted API prompt/response text and associated metadata is 30 days for live logs, then we purge text from active storage. Metadata (non-PHI telemetry like request size, duration, model id) is retained for 13 months for analytics and billing; IPs and API key metadata are retained per our security logs policy (30 days for request logs, 13 months for billing/aggregate). Customers on Dedicated/Private can configure retention and can request shorter windows via support/contract.

3) Storage/backups/analytics: plaintext prompts/responses are not included in long-term backups by default. Backups only contain model binaries and system config; customer inference data is excluded. We do copy short-term request logs to ephemeral analytic pipelines for quality/monitoring — those pipelines are access-controlled and can be turned off for a given account on Dedicated/Private. Any PHI flagged by customer request can be excluded or redacted via configuration.

4) HIPAA / DPA: We will sign a HIPAA-capable DPA for customers requiring it. For Private deployments (VPC or on-prem) we can meet additional controls (customer-managed keys, audited access). For hosted customers, we have a HIPAA DPA template and will engage legal/BD to finalize.

5) Evidence: attaching our redacted SOC 2 Type II (2025) and a concise dataflow diagram that highlights which components persist short-term caches vs ephemeral KV caches. Also providing a 2-3 sentence statement you can include in a DPIA below.

Suggested DPIA statement (short):
"Redwood Inference operates a strict separation between customer inference data and model training pipelines. By default Redwood does not use customer prompts or responses to train or fine-tune production models. Customers requiring model-improvement collaboration may opt-in under a separate agreement, and all such data is de-identified and processed only with explicit customer consent."

Notes: I'll inline the SOC2 link and drive link for the dataflow diagram. If MediCarePlus needs signed paperwork for HIPAA, point them to legal@redwood.ai and we'll fast-track the DPA.

Vivek
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
